statement: From sources/report_excerpt.md, state what the report found about starting parallel candidates instead of continuing sequential repair: the size of the effect, whether it holds across the models tested, and what it costs. Every statement must be supported by the excerpt.
success_criterion: Each assertion is supported by the excerpt, with numbers quoted correctly and no claim broader than the source.
oracles: open sources/report_excerpt.md and confirm each figure and each generalisation against the text and Table 2

submission.claim: The report finds that switching to parallel candidates after two failed rounds raises the resolve rate for three of the four models tested (70.9% to 77.6% for the strongest) and costs two to three times as much per task, while cutting wall-clock time per task by 38% across the models.
assertions: For Large-A the resolve rate rose from 70.9% to 77.6% (+6.7 points) on the 500-task verified subset
The resolve rate improved for three of the four models; for Small-D it fell by 1.2 points
Cost per task was 3.1 times that of sequential repair for Large-A, and 2.4 to 3.3 times for the other models
Wall-clock time per task fell by 38% for the models tested, because the candidates ran at the same time
submission.provenance: Read sections 4 and 5 and Table 2 of sources/report_excerpt.md and quoted the figures.
